However, over the past two years, positive signs around earnings and net effective rental growth have emerged, which management sees as the key catalysts for a share price turnaround. This marks a shift from a period of negative sentiment to one of improving fundamentals, with the balance sheet now positioned well through debt management and portfolio curation.

headline: Australian commercial office market fundamentals set to tighten as new supply becomes unfeasible and obsolescence-led withdrawals shrink net stock

At the same time, obsolescence-led withdrawals will reduce existing stock. This structural supply squeeze, combined with recovering tenant demand, is expected to support net effective rental growth and improve the market outlook over the medium to long term, even as near-term caution around office persists.

headline: Centuria Office REIT's Belinda Cheung points to strong leasing, valuation stabilisation and improving debt costs as catalysts for FY27 earnings growth.
reasoning: Centuria Office REIT delivered FY26 FFO of 11.2 cents per unit and distributions of 10.1 cents, in line with guidance. The portfolio saw ~40,000 sqm of leasing across the year with approximately 5% positive leasing spreads, contributing to a second consecutive year of office valuations stabilising. A refinancing reduced loan margins by ~30 basis points, with no debt expiring until FY28. The sale of 9 Help Street Chatswood at a 12.5% premium to book value and 12.3% IRR was used to repay debt and strengthen the balance sheet. Management has guided FY27 FFO to 11.3 cents per unit and distributions of $0.09 per unit, underpinned by continued leasing momentum and strong capital management.
quote: I think this year we've had some pretty strong results. FY 26, we were able to deliver guidance that we'd announced this time last year. So FFO was 11.2 cents per unit and we paid distributions of 10.1 cents. Um, this was off the back of a number of very successful initiatives that we were able to undertake. First one being great leasing. So we did about 40,000m² of leasing across the portfolio. That's about just under 15% of the entire portfolio. Net lettable area. And a lot of this positive leasing we saw about 5% leasing spreads. So that's positive income growth across the portfolio. And this also led to strong valuation growth in the portfolio. So like we see this portfolio stabilization as a really good sign. It's our second consecutive year of office values stabilizing that coupled with rent growth.
episode_title: Centuria office REIT sees green shoots after profit surge

headline: Centuria Office REIT sees green shoots in office fundamentals as supply constraints and obsolescence withdrawals set to tighten market over medium-to-long term
reasoning: Belinda Cheung argues that while market sentiment around Australian commercial office has been depressed for years, positive signs are emerging in earnings and net effective rental growth. Near-term supply remains manageable, but over the medium and long term, replacement costs are extremely high and development feasibility is deeply challenged, meaning no new stock can be brought to market. Combined with obsolescence-led withdrawals, the overall office market will actually start shrinking, which should support fundamentals. Despite the large discount to NTA and recent distribution cuts, the REIT still offers a 10% distribution yield, and Cheung sees improving fundamentals as the key catalyst for share price recovery.
quote: I think for the office REIT, a huge a huge factor on the share price has really been the market sentiment around commercial office in Australia. It really has had quite a few depressed years. But over the last two years we've seen some really positive signs around earnings and net effective rental growth. There's a lot of tenant demand that is coming back to the market. And I think the key message here is the near-term. The near-term supply is is still looking pretty healthy. But when you look towards the medium and long term replacement costs are so high. Development feasibility is are extremely challenged. No one can bring new stock to the market. On top of that, there's going to be obsolescence led withdrawals of office. So over overall, the office market will actually start shrinking if no new stock is brought to market. So I think over time it's um, the fundamentals are starting to show. Now, you do see those green shoots coming up more and more. So I do think that that will be a major catalyst for the share price. Clearly there is some market caution around office rates overall particularly. I mean look at that divergence between NTA and and unit price. Yeah, there definitely is. There is a big discount at the moment. And despite cutting distributions we still have a very healthy 10% distribution yield.

headline: Centuria's Belinda Cheung flags limited new supply over the next five years as a structural tailwind for commercial office, with Brisbane leading the recovery.
reasoning: Unlike the residential market, commercial office faces very little new supply over the next five years, prompting tenants to lock in space early. Brisbane fringe and metro markets such as Fortitude Valley, South Brisbane and Hamilton are experiencing particularly strong leasing demand driven by the strong Queensland economy and Olympics-related activity in engineering and construction sectors. Leasing spreads in Brisbane are north of 10%, with one deal at an 18% spread, and stronger valuations in Brisbane are beginning to spread to other Australian commercial office markets.
quote: Commercial office is actually really different. The performance of commercial markets is potentially improved after what we've seen happen in the resin market locally. And the few differences would be when you're looking forward over the next five years. There's actually very little new supply coming to the commercial office market. And as a result of that, I think some tenants are realizing that they need to lock in their space now. We've seen that in our portfolio come through really positive leasing. This is particularly strong in the Brisbane market, where there is virtually no supply coming online in the fringe to metro markets. So areas like Fortitude Valley, South Brisbane, even Hamilton, because of the strong economy in Brisbane at the moment driven by the Olympics. There is a lot of growth from tenants that are in that engineering construction sector and so as a result of that, we've seen lots of leasing at really solid leasing spreads as well. Some of these leasing spreads are north of 10%. One of our strongest deals almost for an 18% leasing spread.
episode_title: Centuria office REIT sees green shoots after profit surge
